title: Work and study
job: Explain what you do all day, and how
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE ARTICLE VANISHES BEFORE A BARE PROFESSION. After essere, Italian names a job with nothing in front of it — sono insegnante, sono studente — and English puts an article there every time. Then the article comes STRAIGHT BACK the moment an adjective arrives: sono un bravo insegnante. Both halves run against the English habit, and this is the sentence a work module says most often.

The prepositions of work are convention, not logic, so they are learned as a closed list of four: lavoro IN un ufficio, lavoro PER una ditta, lavoro DA casa, studio ALL'UNIVERSITÀ. in is L1-M7's row doing its usual job; per is new and means "for" in the sense of an employer. There is no rule underneath these — asking why will not help, and the list is short.

DOVERE, POTERE AND VOLERE TAKE A BARE INFINITIVE. devo lavorare, posso studiare, voglio tornare — nothing goes between the two verbs. No to, no di, no che, and never *devo di lavorare. English needs "to" and Spanish needs nothing either, so this is the rare place where Italian is the simpler of the two.

devo is a real verb where L1-M3's vorrei is a frozen piece of politeness. vorrei is one cell of a tense the course has not opened yet (it is L3-M4's); devo, devi, deve, dobbiamo, dovete, devono is a whole present tense that conjugates like any other. L2-M1's posso and L1-M3's voglio are the same kind of verb, met earlier for their own jobs.

An Italian verb owns its preposition and English's does not match. mi occupo DI — you are occupied WITH something — is learned whole, exactly as a phrase and not as a verb plus a choice. The pronoun in front of it is the same reflexive marker L3-M1 opened, and the di after it is not optional.

sentences.cue: I'm a teacher, not a student

words.note: An -e noun, so one shape for a man and a woman and -i in the plural. After essere it stands bare: sono insegnante, with no article at all.

sentences.trap: L1-M1's studente behaves the same way and always did — sono studente carried no article there either. This module is where the pattern is named rather than only shown.
sentences.sound: een-se-NYAN-te. The gn is the ny of onion, and the stress falls on the nyan.

variations.cue: My sister is a teacher
variations.changed: about someone else, and still no article

variations.cue: My brother is a doctor
variations.changed: a different profession, the same bare shape

variations.cue: I'm not a teacher, I'm a student

mistake.display: Sono un insegnante, non sono uno studente
mistake.why: A bare profession takes no article: Sono insegnante, non sono studente.

sentences.usage: The first thing said about yourself at work, and the first place English leaks in.

sentences.display: Sono un bravo insegnante di italiano
sentences.literal: I-am a good teacher of Italian

words.note: A profession like any other, and it follows the same rule: sono medico bare, sono un bravo medico once an adjective is there.

sentences.trap: The adjective is what brings the article back, and nothing else does. Sono insegnante has none; Sono un bravo insegnante has one; and di italiano at the end changes nothing, because it describes the subject taught, not the teacher.
sentences.sound: so-no oon BRA-vo een-se-NYAN-te. bravo takes the stress off the article entirely.

variations.cue: I'm a good teacher
variations.changed: feminine — the noun holds still, the article and adjective move

variations.cue: He's a good doctor
I'm an Italian teacher

mistake.why: An adjective brings the article back: Sono un bravo insegnante.

sentences.usage: Saying what you are good at without a hint of apology, which is normal here.

sentences.display: Lavoro in un ufficio con due colleghi
sentences.cue: I work in an office with two colleagues
sentences.literal: I-work in an office with two colleagues

words.note: The plural drops one i — uffici, not *ufficii — as every -cio noun does. With no article at all, in ufficio means "at work" rather than a particular room.
One shape for both sexes in the singular and two in the plural: colleghi for men or a mixed group, colleghe for women only. The h keeps the g hard.

sentences.trap: A workplace takes in, not a. Vado a casa but lavoro in un ufficio, and the preposition belongs to the phrase rather than to any rule you could work out.
sentences.sound: oof-FEE-cho. The double f is held, and the cio is a soft cho with a silent i.

variations.cue: I work in a small office
I work with two colleagues
variations.changed: an all-female group, so the other plural

variations.display: Il mio capo lavora in ufficio
variations.cue: My boss works at the office
variations.changed: someone else, and no article after in

mistake.display: Lavoro a un ufficio con due colleghi
mistake.why: A workplace takes in: Lavoro in un ufficio con due colleghi.

sentences.usage: Answering where you work, in the first sentence anyone gets.

sentences.cue: I work for an Italian company

words.note: The employer preposition, and the same per already inside L1-M8's per favore and L2-M5's per me. Here it stands alone with a company after it.
What an Italian says for an ordinary business, especially a smaller one. azienda is the word on the letterhead; ditta is the word in the conversation.

sentences.trap: per names who employs you and in names where you are. Lavoro per una ditta and lavoro in una ditta are both correct and mean different things — the first is a contract, the second is a building.
sentences.sound: per OO-na DEET-ta. The double t of ditta is held, and per keeps a clear e.

variations.cue: I work for a big company
I work in an Italian company
variations.changed: in instead of per — the place, not the employer

variations.display: Mia sorella lavora per un bar
variations.cue: My sister works for a bar

mistake.why: An employer takes per: Lavoro per una ditta italiana.

sentences.usage: The half of the question about work that names who pays you.
sentences.mnemonic: per pays you. in houses you.

words.note: One key of two words, with no article inside it — never *da la casa. It is the third of the four work prepositions and the only one with no article after it.

sentences.trap: a casa is going or being home and da casa is working out of it. The two are one letter apart and the preposition is the whole difference.
sentences.sound: da KA-za. The s of casa is a soft z between two vowels.

variations.cue: I usually work from home
I work from home on Mondays
variations.changed: a named day instead of a frequency word

variations.cue: I never work from home
variations.changed: the negative, with L3-M1's non … mai

mistake.display: Qualche volta lavoro da la casa
mistake.why: The phrase carries no article: Qualche volta lavoro da casa.

sentences.usage: The answer everyone now gives to how the week is arranged.

sentences.cue: I have to work on Saturdays too

words.note: A full present tense, unlike L1-M3's vorrei, which is one frozen cell of a tense not yet opened. The verb after it is a bare infinitive with nothing in between.

sentences.trap: Nothing goes between devo and lavorare. English needs "to" and the pull to translate it is strong, but *devo di lavorare and *devo a lavorare are both wrong — the two verbs simply touch.
sentences.sound: DE-vo la-vo-RA-re. Both words are stressed on the syllable before last.

variations.cue: I have to work on Sundays too
We have to work on Saturdays too
I don't have to work on Saturdays

mistake.display: Devo di lavorare anche il sabato
mistake.why: A modal takes the bare infinitive: Devo lavorare anche il sabato.

sentences.usage: Explaining the week you actually have, rather than the one on paper.

sentences.display: Oggi c'è una riunione in ufficio
sentences.cue: There's a meeting at the office today
sentences.literal: Today there-is a meeting in office

words.note: Four syllables, ri-u-nio-ne, with the u fully sounded. An -e noun, so its plural is riunioni.
The word an office actually uses, for a woman as well — il mio capo either way. It also means "head", which is where the sense comes from.

sentences.trap: in ufficio has no article and in un ufficio has one. Bare, it means at work in general; with un, it means inside some particular office — and both appear in this module on purpose.
sentences.sound: ree-oo-NYO-ne. Four syllables, and the i and u are both heard.

variations.display: Oggi c'è una riunione con il capo
variations.cue: There's a meeting with the boss today
There's a meeting tomorrow
There are two meetings today

mistake.display: Oggi c'è una riunione in un ufficio
mistake.why: At work in general is bare: Oggi c'è una riunione in ufficio.

sentences.usage: The line that reorganises a day, said in a corridor.
sentences.mnemonic: in ufficio is at work. in un ufficio is in a room.

sentences.display: Non posso lavorare, devo studiare per un esame
sentences.cue: I can't work, I have to study for an exam
sentences.literal: Not I-can to-work, I-must to-study for an exam

words.note: Masculine despite the -e, so un esame and gli esami. The s between vowels is a soft z: e-ZA-me.

sentences.trap: posso is L2-M1's may-I word doing its plain "can" job here, and it takes the same bare infinitive as devo. One rule covers all three modals — posso lavorare, devo studiare, voglio tornare.
sentences.sound: non POS-so la-vo-RA-re. The double s is held, and the two verbs run together.

variations.cue: I can't go out, I have to study
I have to study for an exam
I can study at home

mistake.display: Non posso di lavorare, devo di studiare
mistake.why: Both modals take the bare infinitive: Non posso lavorare, devo studiare.

sentences.usage: Turning something down with the reason attached, which is the polite shape.
sentences.mnemonic: posso, devo, voglio — all bare after.

sentences.display: Studio all'università e voglio una laurea
sentences.cue: I study at university and I want a degree
sentences.literal: I-study at-the-university and I-want a degree

words.note: ONE key with the elision inside it and a straight apostrophe, answering for nothing else. It is the fourth of the four work prepositions, and the article is compulsory.
Stressed on the first syllable, LAU-re-a, not on the e. It names the qualification; the graduate is a laureato.

sentences.trap: English drops the article — "at university" — and Italian will not. all'università is a fused a + la and it is never *a università.
sentences.sound: al-loo-nee-ver-see-TA. One long run of syllables, with the stress on the final à.

variations.cue: I study Italian at university
I want a degree in Italian
variations.changed: only the second half, with the subject

variations.cue: My sister studies at university

mistake.display: Studio a università e voglio una laurea
mistake.why: The article is fused in and compulsory: Studio all'università.

sentences.usage: The student's half of the same question — what you do all day.
sentences.mnemonic: all'università keeps its article. English does not.

sentences.display: Mi occupo di stipendi in ufficio
sentences.cue: I deal with salaries at the office
sentences.literal: Me I-occupy of salaries in office

words.cue: I deal with · I look after
words.note: One key with its preposition inside it: you are occupied WITH something. The di is not a choice and the phrase is learned whole.
The monthly pay, and the plural drops one i as ufficio's does. It is a neutral office word, not a delicate one.

sentences.trap: The pronoun is L3-M1's reflexive marker again, and it moves with the person — mi occupo, si occupa. What does not move is the di: it is welded to the phrase.
sentences.sound: mee OK-koo-po dee. The double c is held, and the stress is on the ok.

variations.cue: I deal with salaries

variations.display: Il mio capo si occupa di stipendi
variations.cue: My boss deals with salaries
I deal with exams at the university
variations.changed: a different job in a different place

mistake.why: The preposition is part of the phrase: Mi occupo di stipendi in ufficio.

sentences.usage: Saying what you actually do, once the job title has not explained it.
sentences.mnemonic: occupied WITH — the di never leaves.
